findings.description: This bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration and no default bucket encryption. It also stores the vendor-roster workbook object, which is likely to contain vendor/PII data, so objects are persisted in plaintext and readable by anyone with storage access.

The ledger_exports bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so financial ledger exports are written unencrypted. Ledger data is highly sensitive and this fails encryption-at-rest requirements for regulated data.
model_artifacts sets versioning and logging but no server_side_encryption_configuration, so the stored model artifacts are left unencrypted at rest.
ops_runbooks sets versioning but no server_side_encryption_configuration. Runbooks commonly contain internal environment and access details, which are left unencrypted at rest.

No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, so account/bucket-level Block Public Access safeguards are not enforced. A later policy or ACL change could expose this data-bearing bucket publicly without a preventive control in place.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, so Block Public Access is not enforced and a future ACL or policy misconfiguration could expose sensitive ledger data.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, leaving no defense-in-depth guard against accidental public exposure of the stored artifacts.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, so a subsequent ACL/policy change could expose runbook contents that describe internal systems.

No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with the audit log bucket. The bucket also uses the canned log-delivery-write ACL, and without Block Public Access there is no safeguard preventing accidental public exposure of audit data.
